findings.evidence: In .github/workflows/rollout.yml, 'Record rollout recovery' (line ~362) runs before 'Push rollout branch' (~377) and 'Open reviewed rollout PR' (~382). Neither of those later steps has `if: always()` or `!cancelled()`, so they only run if the earlier step succeeded. The diff drops `continue-on-error: true` from the recovery step and adds `set -euo pipefail`, so any record-success failure (label create, issue list, comment or close) now skips the push and PR even though preparation succeeded. The spec text keeps 'SHALL NOT ... affect PR-creation', and the proposal does not call out this side effect. The workflow test only checks that the push/PR `if:` conditions do not mention the streak. It does not catch the implicit step-order dependency. The recovery step should either run after PR creation or be isolated so its failure still surfaces without blocking delivery.
findings.summary: Removing continue-on-error from the 'Record rollout recovery' step lets a tracker error (for example a transient GitHub API failure) stop the rollout PR from being pushed or opened. This breaks the requirement that the tracking layer not affect PR creation.
